quests.instruction: STRIKE THE DRUM PAD CONTAINING THE STRESSED SYLLABLE
quests.hint: Some words in English are spelled identically as a noun and as a verb, but stressed differently. You are hearing the NOUN form of 'suspect'.
quests.explanation: As a noun, 'suspect' stresses the first syllable: SUS-pect. When the same word is used as a verb, the stress shifts to the other syllable (the part that sounds like '...spect'). This noun/verb stress shift is common across dozens of English word pairs - training your ear on it will help you all the way through advanced levels.
quests.stressRule: Noun Stress Rule: Most 2-syllable nouns and adjectives are stressed on the FIRST syllable.
